problems.title: Design a Buffered File Writer

preview.scope: group-level partial preview; no variant-specific text

problems.inferred_spec: An in-memory buffer of fixed capacity sits in front of a byte sink. write appends bytes in order; every time the buffer becomes exactly full it is emptied to the sink in order (so one write may cause several flushes). flush empties whatever is buffered. The provided File/FileSystem sink is modelled as an injected observer: each method returns, as a fresh list, the bytes handed to the sink during that call (empty list if none). The native class also accepts an optional sink object with a write(byte) method.
problems.inferred_domain: capacity 1..10^4; up to 10^4 method calls; each write 0..10^4 bytes, each byte -128..127; total written bytes <= 2*10^5
problems.inference_uncertainty: Whether a full buffer flushes eagerly (assumed) or only when the next byte would overflow; byte range; whether close() exists; real API returns void and side-effects the File.

problems.title: Directory Encryption Optimization

preview.scope: group-level partial preview; no variant-specific text

problems.inferred_spec: The directory tree is given as nested objects (name, directories, files; each file has a name and an isEncrypted flag that is read as the required final state). One operation encrypts a single file or an entire directory subtree. Encryption may never touch a file whose flag is false. Return the minimum number of operations after which exactly the flagged files are encrypted.
problems.inferred_domain: <= 10^5 nodes (directories plus files); depth <= 200 (JSON-transport nesting bound); names [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,30}, unique among siblings
problems.inference_uncertainty: Highest. The preview stops after the node types; the objective (count vs list of paths), whether isEncrypted is current or desired state, and the treatment of empty directories are all inferred.
